rationale:
Evidence from iteration 1 (60 development trials, all tracks): iteration 1 was the best so far (score 111.1, up from 54.0). Oval progress rose from 0.12 to 0.44 and line-loss events fell to zero on the oval. Still no run finished, and every run ended off_track. max_error sits at 0.060 to 0.065 m, which is the off-track limit for this body. rms_error is steady at about 0.028 to 0.033 m on every track, and steering_oscillation is modest (0.16 to 0.27). A steady rms error of about 0.03 m with max error at the limit suggests a persistent lateral bias rather than pure jitter. The likely source is the fixed left/right motor mismatch in the disturbance. kp = 4 with ki = 0.1 cannot cancel a constant offset, so the robot settles off-centre and drifts out on bends. The wider sensor array and larger footprint in iteration 1 clearly helped, so I keep the geometry unchanged to isolate the effect of the controller.

Change: raise ki from 0.1 to 0.5 so the integral term removes the steady bias from the motor mismatch. The integral is clamped to +/-2, so windup is bounded. Everything else (geometry, kp 4.0, kd 0.6, base_speed 1.1, last_direction line loss) is kept the same.

Expected result: lower rms_error (target below 0.02 m) and max_error held clearly under 0.06 m, so off-track events fall and some runs should progress further on the s-bend and slalom. Completion time may stay similar. Risk: a higher ki can add slow overshoot on long bends; if steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35 or rms_error gets worse, the next step is to reduce ki to 0.3 and raise kd.

Hypotheses: H1, a persistent motor-mismatch bias is the main cause of rms_error (about 0.03 m) and the eventual off-track exit. H2, once bias is removed, speed (base_speed 1.1) can be raised in steps of about 0.1 to reach the roughly 1.5 m/s needed to finish in 3 s. Measurements wanted next: rms_error and max_error to test H1, plus progress, completion_time and steering_oscillation to judge how much speed can be added.
